notes.enjala: Le nyaka: want food = be hungry.

guidebook.intro: Food and the market. West Nile is known for cassava (**gbanda**), millet and sorghum bread (**anya**), beans (**osu**) and fish from the Nile.

tips.title: Ma le nyaka
body: To say you are hungry, say you want food: **Ma le nyaka**. Thirsty is **Ma le ii** (I want water).
**Eri adri** is “it is tasty”; add **ndra** for very: **Eri adri ndra!**

tips.title: Ma ovu be
body: **Ma ovu be** is “I have” (literally I am with): **Ma ovu be adripi alu** (I have one brother). Add **ku** at the end to deny it: **Ma ovu be amvipi ku**.
**Ogu** is buy and **ozi** is sell: **Ma ogu nanasi**, **Ma ozi cungwa**.

culture.title: Market day
body: Arua’s markets are full of cassava, groundnuts, simsim, fish and sorghum. People haggle politely and greet the seller before asking a price.
